# Independent code review iteration

Scope: independent full pass over `octolab/config` at `d8771f2` (2022-03-26): all Go source and tests, module metadata, Makefile, lint configuration, GitHub Actions, and README. Existing review files were not used as input; overlap with prior reviews is intentional independent corroboration. Offline issue and roadmap dumps were excluded.

Validation: `GOFLAGS=-mod=readonly go test -race ./...` passed on Go 1.26.5; `GOFLAGS=-mod=readonly go vet ./...` passed; `go test -cover ./...` reported 100% statement coverage for the root package and no tests for `http`.

## 1. The hosted CI runner and artifact transport are no longer available

`.github/workflows/ci.yml:33,50,58,63` and `.github/workflows/tools.yml:18,42` pin every job to `ubuntu-18.04` and the coverage path to `actions/upload-artifact@v3` / `download-artifact@v3`.

GitHub marked the Ubuntu 18.04 hosted image fully unsupported in April 2023, and artifact action v3 has failed on GitHub.com since 30 January 2025. Consequently neither the code workflow nor the tools workflow can provide a green quality gate today; this is not merely an old-version warning. References: [runner removal](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/issues/6002), [artifact v3 shutdown](https://github.blog/changelog/2024-04-16-deprecation-notice-v3-of-the-artifact-actions/).

**Fix.** Move jobs to `ubuntu-24.04` or `ubuntu-latest`, upgrade checkout/setup/cache and artifact actions to supported majors, reduce the matrix to an explicit supported Go policy, and run a manual workflow before re-enabling it as a required check.

## 2. Dependency-only changes bypass every code test

Both `pull_request.paths` and `push.paths` include only the workflow file and `**.go` (`ci.yml:6-15`). A change to `go.mod` or `go.sum` with no Go source change therefore does not trigger tests. That is exactly the shape of a normal dependency update, so a version bump can merge without compilation, race testing, or coverage.

**Fix.** Add exact root patterns `go.mod` and `go.sum` to both triggers, plus `.golangci.yml` and the Makefile when they are part of the gate. Add `tools/go.mod` / `tools/go.sum` to the tooling workflow.

## 3. Lookup cannot distinguish absence from a real zero-valued feature

`Features.FindByID` and `FindByName` return `Feature{}` on a miss. But a zero-valued feature is legal data: an entry may have an all-zero ID or empty name, and a successful lookup of it is byte-for-byte identical to a miss. Callers cannot safely decide whether a feature exists, and adding fields later makes sentinel comparison even more fragile.

**Fix.** Return `(Feature, bool)` (or `*Feature`) and test zero ID, empty name, duplicates, and not-found cases. If duplicate keys are invalid, validate them at construction rather than silently returning the first.

## 4. The supported toolchain and automation are frozen in 2022

The module still declares Go 1.11, CI tests only through 1.18, actions are v2/v3-era, the linter config enables removed linters (`deadcode`, `structcheck`, `varcheck`, `exportloopref`), and the newest commit is from 2022. Current Go 1.26 happens to compile the package, but the repository has no working automation that proves compatibility or vulnerability posture.

**Fix.** First decide whether this package is maintained. If yes, set a realistic minimum Go version, migrate golangci-lint to its current schema, update direct dependencies and Actions, add `govulncheck`, and publish a release documenting the new support floor. Otherwise archive it and point users to the replacement.

## 5. Race-enabled tests have a global one-second deadline

`Makefile:81-88,199-219` defaults `TIMEOUT` to `1s` while both normal and coverage targets enable `-race`. A one-second process-wide timeout is much tighter than the per-test behavior being checked and is sensitive to cold caches, emulation, and shared runners. It turns infrastructure variance into false regressions.

**Fix.** Use a CI timeout in the 30-120 second range and put short deadlines inside the individual tests that require them. Keep the race detector, but do not couple it to a one-second global budget.

## 6. The public documentation still contains placeholder sections

The README's Idea, Motivation, and How-to sections are literal `...`, while the only integration example is `go get`. Users cannot learn what `Feature`, `Secret`, or `http.Server` are for, nor the important fact that serializing `Secret` intentionally destroys its value.

**Fix.** Replace placeholders with a compact API overview and runnable examples for feature lookup, secret redaction, and HTTP server configuration. Document redaction boundaries and the support policy.
